Strategic Partnership Framework 2020 - 2022
The Strategic Partnership Framework (SPF) arƟculates the Regional Centre of Excellence against Hunger and MalnutriƟon (CERFAM) posiƟoning, engagement and partnerships in support to countries’ eﬀorts to accelerate progress towards Zero Hunger in Africa.
The SPF draws from key global and regional strategies and prioriƟes -the Sustainable Development Goal 2030 Agenda, parƟcularly SDG2 - Zero Hunger and the African Union’s Agenda 2063. It is a dynamic overarching framework to guide CERFAM’s partnership approach and work. It lays down robust founda-Ɵons for partnering and incrementally develops a more tailored lens to ﬁne tune its approach and guide its strategic posiƟoning and resource mobilizaƟon eﬀorts.
CERFAM core strengths and capacities
Unique mandateGeographic proximity and extensive networksCatalyst and enabler
CERFAM is mandated to document and disseminate high-impact, evidence-based good pracƟces, soluƟons and innovaƟons generated or adapted to the African context.
South-South and Triangular cooperaƟon plaƞorm
Convening power
CERFAM serves as a plaƞorm for documenƟng, promoƟng and disseminaƟng knowledge, experƟse and know-how to facilitate African countries’ access to proven soluƟons against hunger and malnutriƟon and strengthen capacity and mutual learning.
CERFAM Services Offering
Plaƞorm for exchanges that idenƟﬁes, documents and disseminates good pracƟces and lessons learned to zero hunger.
A catalyst that facilitates the mobilizaƟon and deployment of experƟse for the implementaƟon of good pracƟces against hunger and malnutriƟon through South-South cooperaƟon and country capacity development.
CERFAM’s Unique Value Proposition
Support African countries accelerate progress towards Zero Hunger through a services oﬀering that maximizes the impact of durable local hunger soluƟons
CERFAM does not aim to“do”or“duplicate”exisƟng iniƟaƟves but to“facilitate and create an enabling environment” to connect the demand with the oﬀer to achieve Zero Hunger.
CERFAM can capitalize on its ﬁeldpresence and proximity to governments, insƟtuƟons and partners across Africa to support countries to deliver eﬀecƟve food and nutriƟon programmes.
Reinforced complementariƟes
CERFAM acts as a forum for technical assistance, policy dialogue, advocacy and evidence-based decision making at the conƟnental and regional levels to advance the Zero Hunger agenda.
CERFAM leverages availability, access and uƟlizaƟon of experƟse, lessons learned and experiences from various stakeholders to achieve and sustain shared objecƟves.

Partnership Context
The partnership landscape across the African conƟnent is complex and increasingly evolving, characterized by compeƟng and increasing humanitarian needs, the emergence of non-tradiƟonal partners and the increasing asserƟveness of regional and inter-regional organizaƟons and ﬁnancial insƟtuƟons. Private sector partnership opportuniƟes remain limited across the conƟnent.
Sustainable Development Agenda 2030 and African Union Agenda 2063 urge for a new way of working that fosters an inclusive and holisƟc “whole of society” approach including all relevant stakeholders to build synergies and bring complementariƟes.

CERFAM’s intervenƟons are carried out through inclusive and innovaƟve strategic and operaƟonal partnerships to support naƟonal and regional food security and nutriƟon prioriƟes. These intervenƟons are complemented by policy dialogue, research, technical assistance and advocacy eﬀorts at diﬀerent levels for greater impact and ownership of the Zero Hunger agenda.
Priority areas of collaboration in 2020 – 2022
Support targeted countries to idenƟfy and package their naƟonal soluƟons for food security and nutriƟon and share these good pracƟces, know-how and experƟse with other countries through South-South and triangular cooperaƟon
Disseminate proven good pracƟces for Zero Hunger through robust knowl-edge management, informaƟon systems and capacity development
Facilitate the mobilizaƟon and deployment of technical assistance and the provision of policy advice in country-led eﬀorts and improve the design and implementaƟon of evidence-based hunger soluƟons
The COVID-19 pandemic is having profound economic, social, poliƟcal and environment impacts on many African countries. Its negaƟve consequences on the food security and nutriƟon of the most vulnerable populaƟons call for bold acƟons to meet the food security and nutriƟon requirements of vulnerable populaƟons.
CERFAM has been nurturing a fruiƞul engagement with key stakehold-ers to strengthen its posiƟoning as a facilitator and a partner of choice to governments, naƟonal insƟtuƟons and development partners in Africa in their eﬀorts to achieve Zero Hunger.

Drivers of Success
Branding, CommunicaƟon, and Advocacy strategy brings key messages adapted to target audiences to enhance visibility, demonstrate the impact of intervenƟons, consolidate CERFAM’s credibility as a partner of choice, and aƩract increased support.
Demonstrate the impact of CERFAM’s acƟviƟes through a clear oﬀer of service and evidence-based results that show value for money and achieve greater impact through documenƟng and disseminaƟng good pracƟces and lessons learned.
A Monitoring and EvaluaƟon framework will facilitate the management of acƟviƟes planned, improve their design and implementaƟon, deﬁne realisƟc and concrete targets, measure performance and enhance reporƟng.

Secure stable ﬁnancial resources and mobilize the experƟse and know-how to sustain acƟviƟes on priority themaƟc areas of engagement
Support conƟnental/regional iniƟaƟves through policy support, technical cooperaƟon, capacity development and coordinaƟon including M&E and reporƟng systems. (AUDA-NEPAD, Pan-African universiƟes, ECOWAS, WAHO, RAAF, WECARD, PAIRED, WAAP)
Joint programmes, policy dialogue, advocacy, coordinaƟon, M&E in support to naƟonal, regional and conƟnental zero hunger agenda. Step up collaborƟon with WFP, FAO, IFAD, UNICEF, WHO, UNOSSC, IAEA and others on priority areas
Coordinate and implement complementary technical assistance, expert’s deployment and South-South and Triangular CooperaƟon iniƟaƟves
Promote joint advocacy and mobilize resources. Engage the African Development Bank, the World Bank and the Islamic Development Bank on programmaƟc areas aligned with SDG2
Mobilize funding, technical experƟse, knowledge transfer and capacity strengthening to enhance the capacity of host governments. (SUN Movement and Sun Business Network, CGECI, MEDEF)
Promote inclusive community-based decision making, planning, implementaƟon and monitoring of intervenƟons to strengthen ownership and sustainability
Mobilize knowledge, innovaƟons and networks of experts to generate ﬁeld-tested evidence to inform intervenƟons and capacity strengthening on priority areas. (ICED, Agreenium, CIRAD, CGIAR, universiƟes)
Engage diﬀerent channels to strengthen posiƟoning and visibility with the general public and target audiences
